sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `openclaw`
- Canonical name: OpenClaw (`claim-openclaw-sf-identity`)
- Current status: active public release; latest checked GitHub tag `v2026.7.1-2` (package `openclaw` 2026.7.1-2) published 2026-08-04 (`claim-openclaw-sf-status`, `claim-openclaw-sf-version`, `claim-openclaw-sf-maintenance`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-17
- Vendor: OpenClaw Foundation, a non-profit (`claim-openclaw-sf-vendor`)
- Canonical URL: `https://openclaw.ai` (`claim-openclaw-sf-canonical-url`)
- Repository: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw` (`claim-openclaw-sf-repository-url`)
- Availability: Mac, Windows, or Linux Gateway; companion apps for Windows Hub, macOS menu bar, and iOS/Android mobile nodes; Linux companions planned (`claim-openclaw-sf-availability`)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a personal AI assistant that runs on the operator's devices and meets them in existing chat channels, connecting models, tools, messaging channels, and optional companion apps through one Gateway (`claim-openclaw-sf-unique-value`, `claim-openclaw-sf-architecture-gateway`, `claim-openclaw-sf-execution-location`)
- What it is not: not just a Claude wrapper (`claim-openclaw-sf-not-for-wrapper`); not an IDE replacement (`claim-openclaw-sf-not-for-ide`); not a hostile multi-tenant security boundary for adversarial users sharing one agent or gateway (`claim-openclaw-sf-not-for-multitenant`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` is a catalogue taxonomy inference from first-party agent-runtime / embedded-runner ownership; pages do not use `runtime` as a product-type label (`claim-openclaw-sf-primary-type`)
- Secondary role: `control-plane` — the Gateway is a local / local-first control plane (`claim-openclaw-sf-secondary-role`)
- Agent-loop owner: default model-loop owner is OpenClaw through the OpenClaw embedded runner; if nothing claims the turn in `auto` mode, OpenClaw falls back to `openclaw` as the compatibility runtime (`claim-openclaw-sf-agent-loop-owner`). Codex app-server is a documented alternate model-loop owner (`claim-openclaw-sf-agent-loop-alt`)
- Architecture: a single long-lived Gateway owns messaging surfaces, sessions, auth profiles, channels, and state; everything else is a client (`claim-openclaw-sf-architecture-gateway`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface ledger rows were not written this pass. First-party surfaces in prose:
  - Control UI, CLI, and TUI connect to the Gateway (`claim-openclaw-sf-surface-control`)
  - Messaging channels including WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Signal, iMessage, and others (homepage: 29 channels; docs also list Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Zalo, and channel plugins) (`claim-openclaw-sf-surface-channels`, `claim-openclaw-sf-tag-messaging-channel`)
  - Companion apps: Windows Hub, macOS menu bar, iOS/Android mobile nodes (`claim-openclaw-sf-surface-companions`)
- Execution location: the assistant runs on the operator's devices; tools run on the host unless sandboxing is configured; state lives on the machine, not a vendor cloud (`claim-openclaw-sf-execution-location`, `claim-openclaw-sf-data-path`)
- Platform compatibility: Gateway on Mac, Windows, or Linux; Linux companion apps planned (`claim-openclaw-sf-availability`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: hosted, subscription-backed, gateway, or local models (`claim-openclaw-sf-local-models`, `claim-openclaw-sf-auth-strategy`)
- Auth strategy: API keys (Anthropic/OpenAI/others) or local-only models; Claude Pro/Max and ChatGPT/Codex subscriptions are optional ways to authenticate those providers. First-party pages never use the word BYOK; no `field=byok` claim is written (`claim-openclaw-sf-auth-strategy`)
- Provider support: Anthropic, OpenAI, and others via API keys; optional Claude Pro/Max and ChatGPT/Codex subscription auth; local-only models (`claim-openclaw-sf-auth-strategy`, `claim-openclaw-sf-subscription-reuse`, `claim-openclaw-sf-local-models`)
- Subscription reuse: `supported` (`claim-openclaw-sf-subscription-reuse`)
- Local models: `supported` (`claim-openclaw-sf-local-models`)

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: unknown beyond the documented loop step "context assembly" (`claim-openclaw-sf-session-behavior`)
- Memory: unknown
- Compaction: unknown
- Session behavior: Gateway owns sessions; the agent loop is a serialized per-session run with persistence after inference and tool execution (`claim-openclaw-sf-session-behavior`, `claim-openclaw-sf-architecture-gateway`)

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: typed functions the agent can call, such as `exec`, `browser`, `web_search`, `message`, or `image_generate` (`claim-openclaw-sf-tools`)
- Extensions: unknown as a separate extension model; plugin hooks are documented (`claim-openclaw-sf-hooks`)
- MCP: OpenClaw can consume MCP tools and can expose channel conversations with `openclaw mcp serve` (`claim-openclaw-sf-mcp`)
- Skills: markdown instruction files; OpenClaw follows the AgentSkills spec (`claim-openclaw-sf-skills`)
- Hooks: two systems — Internal hooks (Gateway hooks) and Plugin hooks (`claim-openclaw-sf-hooks`)
- APIs: unknown as a public SDK. Control UI / CLI / TUI and the Gateway WebSocket are client surfaces, not a documented public API product (`claim-openclaw-sf-surface-control`, `claim-openclaw-sf-remote-access`)

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: sandboxing is off by default and controlled by `agents.defaults.sandbox`. Backends: docker, podman, ssh, openshell. The Gateway process always stays on the host; only tool execution moves into the sandbox when enabled (`claim-openclaw-sf-isolation`, `claim-openclaw-sf-tag-sandbox`). Do not flatten this to a single Yes/No.
- Permissions: unknown as a named permission-mode matrix. Default DM pairing: unknown senders get a pairing code and are ignored until approved (`claim-openclaw-sf-security`)
- Security: one user/trust boundary per gateway; not a hostile multi-tenant boundary (`claim-openclaw-sf-security`, `claim-openclaw-sf-not-for-multitenant`)
- Data path: state lives on the operator machine, not a vendor cloud; exact on-disk path unknown (`claim-openclaw-sf-data-path`)

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
Surface ledger rows were not written this pass. Do not treat the prose names below as `surfaces.jsonl` IDs.

- Interface and surfaces in prose:
  - Local Gateway clients: Control UI, CLI, TUI (`claim-openclaw-sf-surface-control`). Local dashboard default `http://127.0.0.1:18789/` (`claim-openclaw-sf-remote-access`)
  - Messaging channels (`claim-openclaw-sf-surface-channels`, `claim-openclaw-sf-tag-messaging-channel`)
  - Desktop companions: Windows Hub, macOS menu bar (`claim-openclaw-sf-surface-companions`)
  - Mobile companion nodes: iOS and Android; they connect to a running Gateway and do not host it (`claim-openclaw-sf-mobile`, `claim-openclaw-sf-mobile-access-ios`, `claim-openclaw-sf-mobile-access-android`)
- Remote behavior: Gateway WebSocket binds loopback port `18789` by default. Remote use is Tailscale Serve, a trusted LAN-Tailnet bind, or SSH forward of the loopback port (`claim-openclaw-sf-remote-access`)
- Mobile behavior: `mobile=supported` via first-party iOS and Android companion node apps. iOS connects over WebSocket (LAN or tailnet) and is not a Codex Computer Use backend. Android is on Google Play and as a signed APK; it requires a running Gateway (`claim-openclaw-sf-mobile`, `claim-openclaw-sf-mobile-access-ios`, `claim-openclaw-sf-mobile-access-android`)
- Background behavior: unknown

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: no OpenClaw product SKU was found. `openclaw.org` says it is free, open source, and belongs to everyone — that is license/OSS, not a pricing claim. No `field=pricing` row is written (`claim-openclaw-sf-license`)
- License: MIT; Copyright (c) 2026 OpenClaw Foundation (`claim-openclaw-sf-license`)
- Maintenance: latest checked release 2026.7.1-2 published 2026-08-04 (`claim-openclaw-sf-maintenance`, `claim-openclaw-sf-version`)
- Lock-in: API keys, optional provider subscriptions, or local-only models; no BYOK word and no `field=byok` claim (`claim-openclaw-sf-auth-strategy`, `claim-openclaw-sf-subscription-reuse`, `claim-openclaw-sf-local-models`)

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: a single-operator personal assistant that meets the user in existing channels and connects models, tools, channels, and companion apps through one Gateway (`claim-openclaw-sf-unique-value`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: sandboxing is off by default, so main-session tools run on the host unless configured (`claim-openclaw-sf-drawback-sandbox-off`, `claim-openclaw-sf-isolation`); not a multi-tenant security boundary (`claim-openclaw-sf-not-for-multitenant`)
- Best fit: developers and power users who want a personal assistant they can message from anywhere without giving up data control or relying on a hosted service (`claim-openclaw-sf-intended-user`)
- Not-for: not just a Claude wrapper; not an IDE replacement; not a hostile multi-tenant gateway (`claim-openclaw-sf-not-for-wrapper`, `claim-openclaw-sf-not-for-ide`, `claim-openclaw-sf-not-for-multitenant`)

claims.claim: Operator-supplied provider API keys are a documented auth path.
Local model providers including LM Studio and Ollama are documented.
OpenClaw connects chat apps to the assistant through channel plugins.
claims.notes: Quote: OpenClaw is a self-hosted gateway that connects your favorite chat apps — Discord, Google Chat, iMessage, Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Signal, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Zalo, and more via channel plugins — to AI coding agents.

claims.claim: First-party mobile node companion apps are documented for iOS and Android.
Sandboxing is a documented optional tool-execution backend.
A tool is a typed function the agent can call, such as exec, browser, web_search, message, or image_generate.
claims.value: typed tools including exec, browser, web_search, message, image_generate
claims.notes: Quote: A tool is a typed function the agent can call, such as exec, browser, web_search, message, or image_generate.

claims.claim: OpenClaw is a single-operator personal assistant that connects models, tools, channels, and companion apps through one Gateway.
claims.value: single-operator personal assistant through one Gateway
claims.notes: Quote: It is designed for a single operator and connects models, tools, messaging channels, and optional companion apps through one Gateway.
